reviewMethod: Primary-source abstract/full-text desk review; not qualified human content approval.

sources.title: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement
sources.population: Children and adolescents; broad evidence synthesis.
sources.supports: Supervised, technique-led, progressive whole-body resistance and power training.
sources.limitations: General training guidance; does not validate each authored variation or a guaranteed change in a soccer test.

sources.title: Position statement on youth resistance training: the 2014 International Consensus
sources.supports: Training should reflect competence, experience and development, with qualified instruction.
sources.limitations: Consensus does not establish a universal age threshold, load or individual readiness score.

sources.title: Resistance Training for Children and Adolescents
sources.supports: Proper technique, suitable equipment and qualified supervision underpin youth resistance training.
sources.limitations: Not proof that independent app instruction replaces observation or qualifies an athlete for a specific load.

sources.title: Overuse Injuries, Overtraining, and Burnout in Young Athletes
sources.supports: Account for combined training and competition, recovery, and regular days without organized training.
sources.limitations: No universal safe workload or injury prediction threshold for an individual child; some recommendations reflect expert opinion.

sources.title: Effects of High-Velocity Resistance Training on Athletic Performance in Prepuberal Male Soccer Athletes
sources.population: 24 male soccer players around 12.8 years; 12-week intervention.
sources.supports: Low/moderate-load resistance training alongside soccer improved selected vertical and horizontal jump outcomes.
sources.limitations: Small male sample; strongest between-group findings concerned jumps. Program effects cannot be assigned to every squat, press, row or hinge variant.

sources.title: Inter-individual Variability in Responses to 7 Weeks of Plyometric Jump Training in Male Youth Soccer Players
sources.population: 76 male soccer players aged 10-16; seven-week jump program plus soccer or soccer alone.
sources.supports: A plyometric program can improve selected jump, sprint, change-of-direction and kicking-distance outcomes.
sources.limitations: Responses vary. Multi-exercise program; not isolated proof for each variation. Kicking distance is not shot speed; no guarantee for girls or all ages10-18.

sources.title: Effects of in-season low-volume high-intensity plyometric training on explosive actions and endurance of young soccer players
sources.supports: Vertical plyometric program improved selected jumping and change-of-direction outcomes.
sources.limitations: 20-m sprint improvement was not significant; vertical jumping evidence must not be promoted as guaranteed sprint improvement.

sources.title: Effects of Contrast Training Using Holding Isometric and Ballistic Exercises on Physical Performance of Youth Male Soccer Players
sources.population: 30 trained male soccer players averaging17.7 years;12 weeks.
sources.supports: Combined holding-isometric and ballistic training improved several physical performance outcomes.
sources.limitations: Cannot isolate isometric effects; does not validate each hold, younger novices, tendon treatment or a universal loading prescription.

sources.title: The Effects of Six-Weeks Change of Direction Speed and Technique Modification Training on Cutting Performance and Movement Quality in Male Youth Soccer Players
sources.population: Non-randomized U17 intervention(n8) and U18 control(n11).
sources.supports: Coached change-of-direction practice can improve cutting time and observed technique.
sources.limitations: Small older-male sample and different age groups; not proof for every pattern, reactive decision making, or injury reduction. Shuttle time alone does not reveal faulty mechanics.

sources.title: Four Weeks of Power Optimized Sprint Training Improves Sprint Performance in Adolescent Soccer Players
sources.population: 24 male players averaging15.7 years; resisted, unresisted and control groups.
sources.supports: Individually loaded resisted sprint training improved short acceleration performance in this study.
sources.limitations: Small study using magnitude-based analysis; not proof for all start styles or a basis for estimating sled load from percentile scores.

sources.title: Reduction of lateral asymmetries in dribbling: the role of bilateral practice
sources.population: Experienced soccer players aged12-14; four months of extensive practice.
sources.supports: Nonpreferred-leg emphasis reduced dribbling-speed asymmetry in the studied program.
sources.limitations: No comparable reduction in kicking asymmetry; does not validate any particular authored move, short dose or overall match-performance claim.

sources.title: Effects of small-sided games and dribbling circuit training on physical and technical skills in youth soccer players
sources.population: 26 highly trained male players around17.5 years; six-week comparison.
sources.supports: Contextual ball/game practice can contribute to technical development alongside physical preparation.
sources.limitations: Older professional-club sample and active comparison; not direct evidence for isolated individual moves or an exact PoseTek dribbling test.

sources.title: Effects of Training with an Agility Ladder on Sprint, Agility, and Dribbling Performance in Youth Soccer Players
sources.population: 18 male players around12.2 years; six weeks.
sources.supports: Counterevidence: no between-group improvement in measured sprint, agility or dribbling outcomes.
sources.limitations: Small trial; included to prevent conflating appealing coordination drills with demonstrated transfer.

sources.title: US Youth Soccer Skills School Manual
sources.population: Youth-soccer skill teaching; not an intervention cohort.
sources.supports: Instructional context for varied receiving, passing and ball-contact techniques.
sources.limitations: Coaching guidance, not causal proof for the authored drills, their doses or athletic-test improvements.

sources.title: How to coach players on passing in football
sources.population: Football coaching across stages; not an intervention cohort.
sources.supports: Different passing contact surfaces and trajectories offer different technical options.
sources.limitations: Official instructional rationale only; does not establish isolated drill effects or transferable test gains.

sources.title: How to coach players on finishing in football
sources.population: Football coaching, including younger and less experienced players.
sources.supports: Varied finishing techniques, manageable distance and a progression from unopposed practice.
sources.limitations: Not an exercise trial. Toe-poke, curl and volley instruction should not be sold as guaranteed improvements in measured shot speed.

sources.title: Jacqueline Duenker: Directing the ball with the first touch
sources.population: Demonstrated youth-girls session; not an intervention cohort.
sources.supports: Body orientation, controlled first touch and movement into space within contextual practice.
sources.limitations: Supports teaching principles, not every authored aerial-control variant or a quantified improvement in the PoseTek dribbling test.
